key_insight: Augmenting scarce optimization datasets with intermediate projected-gradient-descent iterates can improve learning efficiency while admitting a Rademacher-complexity generalization bound that clarifies how k-neighborhood data helps.
engineering_relevance: This provides a data-efficient way to build better warm-start or initial-guess models for expensive parametric optimization problems in DDDAS and related engineering workflows.
method: Collect converged solutions and add solver iterates from a k-neighborhood around each run.
Analyze learnability with a generalization bound based on Rademacher complexity.
Focus the theory and examples on one-sided box-constrained quadratic programs solved by projected gradient descent.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports two illustrative solver examples and a theoretical generalization analysis showing how k-neighborhood size and related parameters affect learning performance.
watch_item: The approach is derived and demonstrated for a specific projected-gradient-descent quadratic-program setting, so performance and bounds may not transfer directly to other solvers or constraint types without adaptation.
paper_title: Complexity Bounds and Approaches to Learning Projected Gradient Descent Solver Iterates
